title: Simulating generic single-qubit open-dynamics via polarization-frequency coupling in a photonic interferometer
authors: Kalle Raikisto, Alberto Ferrara, Tom Kuusela, Rosario Lo Franco, Jyrki Piilo
abstract: We propose a photonic platform for simulating arbitrary single-qubit open-system dynamics using a single photon in an open Mach-Zehnder interferometer. A birefringent quartz plate induces a coupling between the polarization and frequency degrees of freedom. By treating the latter as an effective environment, we analytically derive the reduced polarization dynamics. We show that the resulting evolution is characterized by a controllable interplay between populations and coherence, instead of the usual dephasing caused by quartz plates. By adjusting the photon frequency distribution and interferometric parameters, we demonstrate that target single-qubit states can be efficiently reproduced through a tunable optical protocol expected to work under accessible experimental conditions. The simulator is benchmarked against paradigmatic open-system evolutions, including depolarization and non-Markovian dynamics, achieving high accuracy. Our results establish polarization-frequency engineered photonic interferometers as a versatile protocol for simulation of open quantum systems.
summary: The paper proposes using a single photon interferometer with birefringent quartz to simulate arbitrary open-system dynamics for a qubit encoded in polarization. By treating the frequency mode as an environment, they derive protocols that reproduce complex noise models, including non-Markovian behavior. This establishes the photonic setup as a versatile tool for quantum process simulation.
main_problem: The primary goal is simulating arbitrary single-qubit open-system dynamics using a controllable photonic platform.
main_result: The setup successfully models complex decoherence processes, including non-Markovian dynamics and structured environmental coupling, by engineering the interaction between polarization and frequency degrees of freedom.
method: The authors use an analytical approach involving partial tracing over the continuous frequency environment to derive the reduced density matrix evolution for the qubit polarization state.
model_or_system: The physical system is a single photon propagating through an open Mach-Zehnder interferometer containing a birefringent quartz plate. The qubit is encoded in polarization, and the frequency acts as the effective environment.
key_observables: Qubit populations ($ho_{00}, ho_{11}$) and coherences ($ho_{01}$), detection probabilities ($p_j$), and mean fidelity of the simulation.
important_parameters: Controllable parameters include the spectral width ($\sigma$), mean frequency ($\mu$), quartz thickness ($\ell$), and initial polarization amplitudes ($C_H, C_V$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a Gaussian distribution for the photon frequency spectrum ($|g(\omega)|^2$) and relies on tracing out the continuous frequency degree of freedom.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup (MZI with quartz), show probability distributions vs. tuning parameters ($\mu, \sigma$), and compare simulated qubit evolution against known noise models like depolarization and non-Markovian dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical setup and deriving the initial reduced density matrix via partial tracing over frequency (Appendix A). It then develops the simulation framework by identifying controllable parameters. Finally, it benchmarks the protocol by simulating specific open dynamics, including Markovian damping and non-Markovian coherence revivals.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly versatile, all-optical method for quantum process tomography on qubits, which is crucial for understanding decoherence mechanisms in photonic quantum computing architectures.
